finding.claim: [High, code defect confirmed; impact medium] UpyunCallbackAuth does not abort on signature failure. It writes a 401 but never calls c.Abort() or returns, then calls c.Next(), so the upload-completion handler still runs. The Upyun callback signature check is advisory only.
finding.source: Unauthenticated POST to /api/v4/callback/upyun/:sessionID/:key (attacker controls sessionID, key, body, and signature headers)
finding.sink: callback.ProcessCallback, which completes the upload session and creates the file entity

trace.note: POST callback/upyun/:sessionID/:key registered
UseUploadSession(PolicyTypeUpyun) loads the session by sessionID and key
UpyunCallbackAuth is the only provider-auth middleware in the chain
upyun.ValidateCallback returns err for a bad signature
c.JSON(401,...) is written, but there is no return and no c.Abort()
c.Next() runs unconditionally, so the remaining handlers execute
ProcessCallback runs and completes the upload
ProcessCallback calls callback.ProcessCallback(c) and returns 200 on success

finding.guards_checked: (1) UseUploadSession: session lookup by sessionID and key; implementation is not in this repo, so unverified. (2) upyun.ValidateCallback: signature verification; not in this repo, but its error is observed correctly here. (3) c.Abort()/return after the 401: absent, so the guard fails open. Precondition: the attacker must hold a valid sessionID and key for a pending Upyun upload session (normally the uploader, or anyone who sees the callback URL). Impact is limited to completing a session without the provider's signed proof of upload, for example with spoofed size or metadata, if ProcessCallback trusts the body.

finding.claim: [Plausible] The OneDrive, COS, S3, KS3 and OBS upload-completion callbacks have no provider-verification middleware, while remote, OSS, Upyun and Qiniu do. Only the path-borne key gates them. The GET variants (COS, S3, KS3) complete uploads with the key in the URL, where it can leak to logs and Referer headers.
finding.source: Unauthenticated POST/GET to callback/onedrive/:sessionID/:key, callback/obs/:sessionID/:key, or GET callback/cos|s3|ks3/:sessionID/:key
finding.sink: callback.ProcessCallback, which completes the upload session

only UseUploadSession(PolicyTypeOd) before ProcessCallback
GET cos/:sessionID/:key, only UseUploadSession (518) then ProcessCallback
GET s3/:sessionID/:key, only UseUploadSession (524)
GET ks3/:sessionID/:key, only UseUploadSession (530)
POST obs/:sessionID/:key, only UseUploadSession (536)
contrast: remote has RemoteCallbackAuth (479)
contrast: oss has OSSCallbackAuth (486) and OSSCallbackValidate (487)
contrast: qiniu has QiniuCallbackValidate (543)

finding.guards_checked: UseUploadSession (session and key lookup) only. Whether the key is a high-entropy secret and whether ProcessCallback verifies the object actually exists in the bucket is in service code not present here. Impact is unverified until those are read.

finding.claim: [Medium, confidence medium] Direct-link creation (PUT file/source) and deletion (DELETE file/source/:id) are gated only by files.read scope. A read-only token can publish files at the anonymous /f/:id/:name endpoint. Creating a public link is a share-like publish action; share creation requires shares.write.

finding.sink: explorer.GetDirectLinkService.Get / explorer.DeleteDirectLink, which create or delete anonymously reachable links

finding.guards_checked: RequiredScopes(FilesRead) at 601. ValidateBatchFileCount on the batch size only. Owner check for DeleteDirectLink and GetDirectLinkService is not visible here and must be verified in service code.

finding.claim: [Plausible, needs service verification] PATCH user/setting is gated only by UserInfoWrite. Passkey and security-sensitive operations use UserSecurityInfoWrite elsewhere. The legacy commented-out dispatcher in user.go still routes password, 2fa, and authn changes through this endpoint. If PatchUserSetting still accepts those fields, a token lacking the security scope can change credentials.
finding.source: Bearer token with user.info:write scope, sending a PATCH body with credential-related fields
finding.sink: usersvc PatchUserSetting.Patch (service layer, not in repo), reached via controllers.UpdateOption

setting.Use(RequiredScopes(UserInfoRead))
PATCH setting
RequiredScopes(UserInfoWrite) is the only scope gate
UpdateOption passes the body to PatchUserSetting.Patch
legacy dispatch lists password, 2fa, and authn as options handled here
contrast: passkey routes require UserSecurityInfoWrite

finding.guards_checked: LoginRequired (auth group, router.go:869); RequiredScopes(UserInfoWrite) at 1282. Whether PatchUserSetting accepts password, 2FA, or authn fields and whether it re-checks the password or scope is not visible.

finding.claim: [Confirmed code defect, low severity] BatchDeleteShare has no return after the error branch. On failure it writes the error JSON and then writes a success JSON body with HTTP 200, so the client can see both, and a failed batch delete can read as successful.
finding.source: Authenticated user submitting a batch delete whose service call fails
finding.sink: HTTP response to the client (misreported success)

closing brace with no return or Abort
c.JSON(200, Response{}) writes success after the error

finding.guards_checked: None needed; the defect is in the error path. No security impact on authorization is shown. Business-logic impact is that failed deletes are reported as successful.

finding.guards_checked: None visible. Whether the path is logged, and whether the password is stored or hashed, is unverified.
